title: Deep neural networks as lattice gauge theories
abstract: We modify the NN/QFT duality [1] to incorporate the layerwise permutation symmetry of the network, resulting in a $(0\!+\!1)$-dimensional lattice gauge theory, in which each layer of $N$ neurons acts as an $N$-component lattice site, and the weight matrices play the role of gauge fields living on the links. In this framework, we compute the tree-level neuron-neuron propagator which describes the evolution of layer variance in the network, and develop the Feynman diagram machinery to compute interactions in the perturbative expansion in $1/N$. In particular, we obtain a recursive expression for all corrections to the exact propagator at $O(1)$, representing statistical fluctuations in the ensemble of networks, including infinitely-many loop diagrams mediating the interactions from previous layers. We also present a preliminary analysis of neuron scattering amplitudes that contribute order-by-order in $1/N$, which provides a field-theoretic framework for studying higher-point correlations, and by extension information propagation, in deep networks. We remark on some interesting directions for future work at the intersection of neural networks and quantum field theory.
summary: This work reformulates deep neural networks as a $(0+1)$-dimensional lattice gauge theory by incorporating the layerwise permutation symmetry. Using techniques from quantum field theory, the authors compute propagators and scattering amplitudes in the large-$N$ limit. This provides a powerful, rigorous field-theoretic framework for studying information flow and correlations within deep learning models.
main_problem: The paper modifies the NN/QFT duality to incorporate the layerwise permutation symmetry of deep neural networks, treating the network as a lattice gauge theory.
main_result: They develop a field-theoretic framework to compute the neuron-neuron propagator and scattering amplitudes in the perturbative expansion in $1/N$, providing insights into information propagation.
method: The methodology involves adapting lattice gauge theory concepts to a discrete symmetry group ($S_N$), calculating the partition function via path integrals, and performing large-$N$ expansions.
model_or_system: The model is a deep neural network (MLP) treated as a $(0+1)$-dimensional lattice gauge theory, where layers are sites and weight matrices act as link variables.
key_observables: Neuron-neuron propagator, layer variance evolution, neuron scattering amplitudes, and correlation functions.
important_parameters: Network width ($N$), layer index ($\ell$), and the large-$N$ limit ($1/N$ expansion).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to random networks at initialization, and the continuum limit is avoided due to the discrete nature of the symmetry.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the lattice gauge theory formulation based on $S_N$ symmetry, through the calculation of the partition function using auxiliary fields, and finally to developing the perturbative machinery for computing propagators and correlation functions.
why_interesting: The connection between the discrete symmetries of neural networks and the mathematical machinery of lattice gauge theory provides a novel, field-theoretic lens for understanding complex information processing dynamics.
